title: The five pillars of managing menopause
summary: Learn about the effects of menopause and perimenopause and get clear guidance on symptoms, the onset of them, lifestyle strategies and treatment options that can improve your employees’ overall well-being.
body_markdown:
October is[Menopause Awareness Month](https://www.imsociety.org/education/world-menopause-day-2026/) , a time to increase understanding of a life transition that[affects millions of women](https://www.oviahealth.com/menopause/) . Open conversations can help normalize these experiences, connect your employees with reliable information, and support informed decisions about health and well-being.


The goal of health observances is to provide public education, improve resources, and shed light on health journeys. Speaking about menopause symptoms can help break down social taboos and highlight effective health strategies.


## Menopause basics


Menopause doesn't happen overnight. The transition typically begins with perimenopause, which often[starts between ages 45 and 55](https://www.nia.nih.gov/health/menopause/what-menopause) , although it can happen earlier or later with some women.


During this stage, estrogen and progesterone levels fluctuate, leading to irregular menstrual cycles and symptoms that can vary widely from person to person. Menopause is defined as 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period and occurs at an average age of 52 years in the U.S.


## Eight signs of perimenopause and menopause


[Common symptoms include:](https://www.nia.nih.gov/health/menopause/what-menopause)


- Hot flashes
- Brain fog
- Night sweats
- Mood changes
- Joint discomfort
- Vaginal dryness
- Sleep disturbances
- Changes in sexual health


Symptoms can begin before noticeable changes in menstrual cycles, often starting in a woman's 40s. They can vary substantially from person to person and may warrant clinical review if they’re disruptive or occur unusually early. For some, they can affect work, relationships, exercise routines, sleep quality, and overall quality of life.


**The good news is that effective strategies are available. Evidence-based approaches include:**


- Lifestyle modifications
- Hormone therapy
- Nonhormonal medications
- [Symptom tracking](https://www.oviahealth.com/guide/105891/health-tracking-symptoms/)
- Personalized care plans developed with a healthcare provider


## The five pillars of managing menopause


Menopause brings physical, emotional, and psychological shifts. Your employees can navigate them by focusing on these five pillars of lifestyle management:

Prioritizing these areas protects long-term heart and bone health while helping keep hormones and daily symptoms in balance. Partnering with an OB-GYN or primary care provider allows your employees to access the science-backed, professional guidance they deserve during this transition.


#### 1. Nutrition


Emphasizing whole, nutrient-rich foods and minimizing processed foods may reduce hot flashes, enhance energy and mood levels, and[protect long-term health](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10780928/) by supporting bone health and preventing heart disease. Other nutrition tips include:


- Focusing on a balanced diet rich in calcium, vitamin D, lean protein, and healthy fats to reduce inflammation, while limiting caffeine and added sugars
- Eating cooling, hydrating fruits and vegetables like watermelon and cucumbers to help reduce body temperature and drinking chilled water throughout the day
- Limiting alcohol and spicy foods, which may trigger or worsen hot flashes


#### 2. Exercise


A consistent exercise plan during menopause may[help ease symptoms](https://www.urmc.rochester.edu/news/publications/health-matters/why-exercise-is-essential-during-menopause) like joint pain, weight gain, and poor sleep quality. It also benefits bone health and reduces the risk of chronic conditions like heart disease and diabetes.


Suggest your employees:


- Engage in strength-training exercises at least twice per week
- Consider trying yoga, tai chi, or Pilates to improve flexibility, build core stability, and support mental well-being
- Aim for 150 minutes each week of moderate cardiovascular exercise like brisk walking, cycling, or swimming, or 75 minutes of vigorous activity, such as running


#### 3. Sleep


Rest acts as a counterbalance to fatigue and stress. The body copes better with hormonal shifts when[sleep is adequate](https://www.ncoa.org/article/menopause-and-sleep-what-every-woman-should-know/) . Other benefits include mood stabilization and protection of overall health.


Sleep tips include:


- Keeping a regular sleep schedule
- Practicing good[sleep hygiene](https://www.sleepfoundation.org/sleep-hygiene)
- Sleeping in light layers
- Cooling down the bedroom before bedtime
- Finding a relaxing sleep routine or ritual
- Aiming for at least seven hours of sleep per night


#### 4. Stress control


[Stress](https://themenopausecharity.org/information-and-support/what-can-help/self-care/stress-management-in-menopause/) increases cortisol levels, which may worsen mood swings, fatigue, hot flashes, and insomnia. Tips to control stress include:


- Confronting and reframing negative thoughts
- Tracking daily symptoms to spot personal triggers
- Releasing outdated expectations and habits like people-pleasing
- Practicing[breathwork](https://www.lung.org/blog/stress-breathing-exercises) to manage stress and calm the nervous system
- Embracing menopause as a time of growth and self-discovery, recognizing the strengths and wisdom gained through life experience


#### 5. Care and connections


Quality medical care remains essential throughout life's journey. A physician can address specific symptoms and concerns with personalized treatment tailored to your employees’ health history.


Complementing this clinical care, fostering meaningful relationships builds a strong support network that relieves stress and boosts emotional well-being. Have your employees consider:


- Partnering with a medical team to get a personalized, evidence-based care plan that includes hormone replacement therapy, if warranted
- Establishing meaningful networks to buffer against daily pressures and foster emotional resilience
